gap: No result ChatGPT got states how much filament a colour change wastes. Notebookcheck measured it on the Bambu Lab X2D: 70 g of waste for a 12 g multicolour Benchy on one nozzle (5.8 g wasted per gram printed) and 20 g on both nozzles (1.7 g per gram), which is 71% less waste. Print time fell from 5.8 h to 2.7 h.
standout_why: I compared against desktop3dprinters.us/lists/multicolor-enclosed-3d-printers (cited). It has launch price, multi-material system, nozzle count, enclosure, max chamber temperature and build volume for 23 printers. It has no purge, flush or waste column. Slot counts appear only in its text, and price per litre and price per slot can be worked out from its table, so a cost-per-slot figure would not stand out. Neither that page nor ChatGPT's answer gives grams of waste per colour change or waste per gram of model. ChatGPT's answer calls the H2D 'better for complex multi-material work' without a number. The second cited result, 3dprinterlist.com, would not load (TLS certificate error), so I could not check it.
decides: It backs ChatGPT's split with a number. A single-nozzle feeder machine (P1S/P2S Combo, Creality K2 Pro Combo, QIDI Q2 + QIDI Box) is fine for occasional 2–4 colour prints. On a small, swap-heavy multicolour model, one nozzle threw away about 5.8 g per gram of part against about 1.7 g with two nozzles. Someone printing lots of small multicolour parts gets back part of the extra cost of a dual-nozzle Bambu (X2D/H2D) in filament and roughly half the print time. The measurement was taken on the X2D, not the H2D.

findings.label: Filament wasted per gram of model, multicolour Benchy, one nozzle
findings.value: 5.8 g waste per g printed (70 g waste for a 12 g model)
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab X2D in detail: Dual-nozzle halves printing time and drastically reduces waste (Notebookcheck, Silvio Werner)
findings.note: Silvio Werner (Notebookcheck) measured about 70 g waste per 12 g model, 52 g of it from flushing. 70 / 12 = 5.8 g/g. Model: 3Designs Multicolor-3D-Benchy. Published 2026-06-10, updated 2026-10-05. This was the X2D run on one nozzle, used as a stand-in for single-nozzle feeder printers such as the P2S or K2 Pro; those printers were not tested.

findings.label: Filament wasted per gram of model, same Benchy, both nozzles
findings.value: 1.7 g waste per g printed (20 g waste for a 12 g model)
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab X2D in detail: Dual-nozzle halves printing time and drastically reduces waste (Notebookcheck, Silvio Werner)
findings.note: About 20 g waste, mostly the purge tower. 20 / 12 = 1.7 g/g. Reduction against one nozzle: (70 − 20) / 70 = 71%.

findings.label: Print time, same Benchy, one nozzle vs both nozzles
findings.source_title: Bambu Lab X2D in detail: Dual-nozzle halves printing time and drastically reduces waste (Notebookcheck, Silvio Werner)
findings.note: (5.8 − 2.7) / 5.8 = 53%. Notebookcheck also got 1.7 h with priming turned off but said print quality suffered.

findings.label: Purge per colour change in QIDI's own worked example
findings.value: 0.19 g PLA per change (150 mm³); 100 changes ≈ 19 g
findings.source_title: How to Set Up Multi-Color 3D Printing With QIDI Box (QIDI guide)
findings.note: QIDI's example: 100 changes at 150 mm³ ≈ 19 g PLA, at 1.24 g/cm³. 0.150 cm³ × 1.24 = 0.19 g per change. QIDI says QIDI Studio sets the purge for each colour pair, so this is an illustration, not a measurement. Same page: 4 filaments per QIDI Box, up to 4 boxes per printer (16 colours or materials).
